                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXIX</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1. <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Oh Ariel,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>the lion of God.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> WO to <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This Word signifies <ns0:hi>a strong Lion,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>the Lion of God;</ns0:hi> and is used<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> concerning <ns0:hi>Lion-like</ns0:hi> Men, as it is rendred, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 11. 22. and of God's <ns0:hi>Altar,</ns0:hi> as it is rendred, <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 43. 15, 16. which seems to be thus called, because it de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voured and consumed the Sacrifices put upon it as gree<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dily, and as irresistably, as the Lion doth his prey. If the Altar be here meant, it is put Synecdochically for the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, and the words may be rendred, <ns0:hi>Wo to Ariel, to Ariel</ns0:hi> of or in <ns0:hi>the City,</ns0:hi> or, and <ns0:hi>the City;</ns0:hi> for that conjunction is sometimes understood, as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 22. 6. <ns0:hi>Hab.</ns0:hi> 3. 11. And so the Threatning is denounced both against the Temple, and against <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> But he seems rather to understand it of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> as may be gathered: 1. From the next words, which seem to be added by way of Apposition, to explain what he meant by that obscure and ambiguous Term: <ns0:hi>Wo to Ariel, to Ariel,</ns0:hi> even to <ns0:hi>the City:</ns0:hi> 2. From the following Verses, which plainly declare, That this <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> is the place which God threatens, that he would <ns0:hi>distress</ns0:hi> and fill with <ns0:hi>heaviness, ver.</ns0:hi> 2. and <ns0:hi>lay siege</ns0:hi> against Her, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 3. And that <ns0:hi>the Nations</ns0:hi> should <ns0:hi>fight against her, ver.</ns0:hi> 7. All which Expressions agree much better to <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem,</ns0:hi> than to the Altar. And this City might be called <ns0:hi>Ariel,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>the strong Lion:</ns0:hi> Either 1. For its eminent strength in regard of its Scituation and Fortifications, by reason whereof, it was thought almost impregnable, both by them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves and others, <ns0:hi>Lam.</ns0:hi> 4. 12. Or, 2. For its Lion-like Fierceness and Cruelty, for which she is called <ns0:hi>the bloody City, Ezek.</ns0:hi> 7. 23. and 22. 2. and in effect, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1. 15. and 59. 3. and <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 19. 4. and for which her Princes are cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>Lions, Ezek.</ns0:hi> 19. 2. <ns0:hi>Zeph.</ns0:hi> 3. 3. Or. 3. In respect of the Altar of God, which was Erected in, and confined to that City, and in which the Strength and Glory of that City did chiefly consist.</ns0:note>, to <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> of the ci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty.</ns0:note> the city <ns0:hi>where David</ns0:hi> dwelt <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The Royal City, and Seat of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and his Posterity. Which is here mentioned, as the ground of their Confidence; and withal, it is imply<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, That their Relation to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and their supposed In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terest in the promises made to him, and to his Seed, should not secure them from the Destruction here threat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned.</ns0:note>: add ye year to year; let them <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> cut off the heads.</ns0:note> kill sacrifices <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Go on in killing Sacrifices from time to time, one year after another, whereby you think to appease me, and to secure your selves: But all shall be in vain.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2. Yet <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Notwithstanding all your Sacrifices.</ns0:note> I will distress <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">By bringing and strengthning her Enemies against Her.</ns0:note>, and there shall be heaviness and sorrow, and it shall be unto me as <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Sense is, Either 1. I will treat Her like a strong and fierce Lion, which the People, among whom it is, indeavour by Nets, or Pits, and all other ways to take and to destroy. Or. 2. I will make <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> the City, like <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> the Altar, filling it with Sacrifices, even with Men, whom I will Slay in my Anger; which Act of God's is called <ns0:hi>his Sacrifice, Ezek.</ns0:hi> 39. 17, 19.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3. And I will camp against thee <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> with an army.</ns0:note> round a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout, and will lay siege against thee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">By those Enemies whom I will assist, and enable to Destroy thee. This was fulfilled, Either 1. by <ns0:hi>Sennache<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rib,</ns0:hi> as some Learned Men think. But what is here affirm<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed of these Enemies, is expresly denied concerning <ns0:hi>Senna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cherib, Isa.</ns0:hi> 37. 33. or rather 2. by the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 25. 1. &c.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> with a setled camp, or leaguer.</ns0:note> with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4. And thou shalt be brought down, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Thou who now speakest so loftily, and scornfully against the Lord's Prophets and others, shalt be humbled and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />founded, & afraid & ashamed to speak aloud, & shalt in a sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />miss manner, and with a low Voice, beg the favour of thine Enemies.</ns0:note>, and thy voice shall be as of one that hath a familiar spirit out of the ground <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Who, that they might possess the People with a kind of Reverence and Horror, used to speak and deliver their Answers with a low Voice, either out of their Bel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lies, or from some dark Cave under the ground.</ns0:note>, and thy speech shall <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>peep,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>chirp.</ns0:hi> Chap. 8, 19.</ns0:note> whisper out of the dust.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5. Moreover, the multitude of thy strangers <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either 1. of the Strangers that Encamp and Fight against thee. Or, 2. of the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> and other Strangers, whom thou hast hired to assist thee, as indeed they did, when the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans</ns0:hi> came against them. This Exposition seems to agree best, as with the phrase, <ns0:hi>thy strangers,</ns0:hi> so with the scope of the place, and with the whole Context, especially the foregoing Verses; which plainly shews, that this is not a Promise to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> but a Threatning against it.</ns0:note> shall be like small dust <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Quickly blown away with the least Wind, by comparing this with the following Clause.</ns0:note>, and the multitude of the terrible ones <ns0:hi>shall</ns0:hi> be <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job. 21. 18. Chap. 17. 13.</ns0:note> as chaff that passeth away: yea it shall be <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This dissipation and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction of thy Strangers, and terrible Ones shall come to pass.</ns0:note> at <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 30. 13.</ns0:note> an instant suddenly.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>b</ns0:hi> Of thy great Comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders, and stoutest Souldiers.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6. Thou <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Thou, O <ns0:hi>Ariel</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> of, or to whom this whole Context manifestly speaks.</ns0:note> shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">With dreadful Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, which are frequently expressed in the Prophets, by these and such like Metaphors.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7. And the multitude of all the nations that fight against <ns0:hi>Ariel,</ns0:hi> even all that fight against her, and her munition, and that distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Wherein it shall be so, is explained in the next Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8. It shall even be as when a hungry <ns0:hi>man</ns0:hi> dreameth, and behold he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">His appetite or desire (as <ns0:hi>the soul</ns0:hi> is taken, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 41. 4. and 78. 18. and elsewhere) is unsatisfied. Or, his stomack or body (as <ns0:hi>the soul</ns0:hi> is used, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 16. 10.) is empty.</ns0:note>: or as when a thirsty <ns0:hi>man</ns0:hi> dreameth, and behold he drinketh; but he awaketh, and behold <ns0:hi>he is</ns0:hi> faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">No less unsatisfied and insatiable, shall the Enemies of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> be, with all the Cruelties which they have commit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted against you; and they shall be alwayes thirsting af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter more of your Blood, as if they had never tasted any of it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9. Stay your selves and wonder <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Pause upon it, and you will see cause to wonder at the stupidity of this People, of which he is now about to speak. He directeth his Speech, either to the Religious part of the People, or to those particular persons, who heard him, when he delivered this Prophecy.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> take your pleasure and riot.</ns0:note> cry ye out, and cry <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Cry out again and again, either in way of Supplication for them; or rather through Astonishment and Horror. Or, <ns0:hi>They take pleasure</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>sport themselves</ns0:hi> (as this word most commonly signifies) <ns0:hi>and riot:</ns0:hi> In the midst of all these Threatnings and Dangers, they are secure, and give up themselves to sen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />suality; which is matter of just wonder.</ns0:note>: they are drunken, but not with wine <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">But either 1. With drinking the Cup of God's fury, wherewith they are said to be made drunk, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 51. 17, 20. And then <ns0:hi>they are drunk,</ns0:hi> is put for, <ns0:hi>they shall be drunk,</ns0:hi> after the manner of the Prophets. Or 2. With the spirit of giddiness or stupidity, which makes them like drunken Men, insensible of their Danger, and not knowing what to do.</ns0:note>; they stagger, but not with strong drink.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 11. 8.</ns0:note> the LORD hath poured out upon you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Which Phrase notes the plenty, and vehemency of this Judgment.</ns0:note> the spirit of dead sleep <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Hardness of heart, and insensibleness of your Danger and Misery, which God is said to send, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause He denies, or withdraws His Light and Grace, which alone can cure those Maladies.</ns0:note>, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> heads.</ns0:note> rulers, the seers <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Your Magistrates and Ministers, whose blindness or stupidity is a great Curse and Plague to the people. Or, <ns0:hi>the Prophets, even the chief</ns0:hi> (for <ns0:hi>the head</ns0:hi> is oft put for the chief of persons or things, as <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30. 23. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 12. 18. and elsewhere) <ns0:hi>of your seers.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> hath he covered <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">With the veil of ignorance and stupidity, or as to their Eyes, which is understood out of the former Clause. And this last Clause is, and may be rendred thus, The Eyes (which<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> may be repeated out of the foregoing Clause) <ns0:hi>of your Prophets, and of,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>even of your principal seers</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>and of your most intelligent rulers.) hath he covered.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11. And the vision of all <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Of all your Prophets, whether the true of false Ones.</ns0:note> is become unto you, as the words of a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> letter.</ns0:note> book <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> is sealed <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">In which no Man can read, whilst it is scaled up, as books then sometimes were, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 21. 8. <ns0:hi>Esth.</ns0:hi> 3. 12, 13. being made in the form of Rolls, which was convenient for that purpose.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>men</ns0:hi> deliver to one that is learned, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:591" />
Read this, I pray thee; and he saith, I cannot, for it <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> sealed:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12. And the book is delivered to him that is not learned <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Unsealed and opened, as the follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Clause implies. God so orders the manner of deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vering this Book, that neither the learned nor unlearned could read and understand it.</ns0:note>, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13. Wherefore the LORD said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 33. 31. Mat. 15. 8. Mar. 7. 6.</ns0:note> Forasmuch as this people draw near <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To wit, in acts of worship.</ns0:note> with their mouth, and with their lips <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">With outward Devo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, and the profession of Religion.</ns0:note> do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">They do not pay Me that Love, and Fear, and Obedience, which I require, and prefer before all Sacrifices, and external Services.</ns0:note>, and their fear towards me is taught by the precept of men <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">They Worship Me not in such way and manner, as I have commanded and prescribed, but according to their own, and other Mens inventions, preferring the devices and tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ditions of<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> their false Prophets, before My Institutions. For this was a common Errour among the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> as we learn from <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 7. 31. <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 5. 11. and many other Scriptures, And thus our blessed Saviour expounds this very place, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 15. 7, 8, 9.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14. Therefore behold, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> I will add.</ns0:note> I will proceed to do a marvellous work amongst this people, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> a marvellous work and a wonder, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 49. 7. Obad. ver. 8. 1 Cor. 1. 19.</ns0:note> for the wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of their wise <ns0:hi>men</ns0:hi> shall perish, and the un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstanding of their prudent <ns0:hi>men</ns0:hi> shall be hid <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Shall disappear and vanish; for this answers to, <ns0:hi>shall perish,</ns0:hi> in the former Clause. A veil shall be cast upon the Eyes of their Minds: they shall give no evidences or proofs of their Wisdom, but their Folly shall be made manifest. And this was indeed a wonderful Thing for their wise Men to be made fools.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 30. 1.</ns0:note> Wo unto them that seek deep <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb. that make deep.</ns0:hi> A Metaphor from Men, who use to dig deep into the Earth, that they may hide any thing there, which they would keep safe and unknown.</ns0:note> to hide their counsel from the LORD <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Vain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly imagining, That they can keep all their Hypocrisy and secret Wickedness out of God's fight, and that they can deceive, not onely Men, but God, by their external Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fessions and Services.</ns0:note>, and their works are in the dark <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Their wicked Counsels are con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trived, and their Idolatry is practised in secret and dark places, of which, see <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 8. 12.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 94. 7.</ns0:note> they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">We act so cunningly, that neither God nor Man can discover us.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16. Surely your turning of things upside down <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">All your subtile devices, by which you turn your selves into all shapes; and turn your Thoughts hither and thi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and pervert the order which God hath appointed.</ns0:note> shall be esteemed as the potters clay <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">It is no more to me, than the Clay is to the Potter, who can not onely discern it thoroughly, but alter and dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose it as he seeth fit.</ns0:note>: for shall the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 45. 9.</ns0:note> work say of him that made it, He made me not, or shall the thing framed, say of him that framed it, He had no understanding <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And no less absurd and ridicu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lous is your Conceit, that I your Maker, and supream Governor, cannot discover, and controul all your Artifices at my Pleasure.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17. <ns0:hi>Is</ns0:hi> it not yet a very little while, and <ns0:hi>Lebanon</ns0:hi> shall be turned into a fruitful field: and the fruit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful field shall be esteemed <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 72. 16.</ns0:note> as a forrest? <ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>h</ns0:hi> The Forrest of <ns0:hi>Lebanon,</ns0:hi> which was a barren Mountain, and a desolate Wilderness, shall, by God's wonderful provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence, become a fruitful and populous Place; and these pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces which are now Fruitful and Populous, shall then be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />come as Barren and Desolate, as that Forrest.                   </ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="19">19. The meek <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The humble and meek Believers, opposed to those proud and scornful <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> of whom He speaks in this, and in the foregoing Chapter.</ns0:note> also <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
